title: Hybrid backoff profiles, idempotency scoping, and streaming-safe retry taxonomy for SDKs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Produce a cross-language recommendation and default configuration set that balances latency, cost, and correctness for SDK retries. Scope: Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs; unary and streaming endpoints; hosted and private deployments. Deliverables: (1) A small set of named backoff profiles (latency-first, balanced, throughput/cost-first) with concrete parameter defaults, (2) Idempotency key semantic guide (scope, lifetime, generation helpers) including streaming-safe variants, (3) Retryable error taxonomy and mapping to retry profiles (transient vs permanent vs client-correctable), (4) Example idiomatic code snippets for Python/TS/Go demonstrating common patterns (upload/chunked, interactive chat, long-polling/resume), and (5) Tests and integration checklist to validate behavior across runtime and weekend-failover scenarios. Acceptance criteria: Clear defaults shipped in SDKs, backward-compatible opt-out, unit + integration tests for streaming resume and duplicate suppression, and documentation + migration guide for customers planning to adopt reserved capacity or private deployments.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Maya Chen: Created ticket after sync with DX and Platform teams. Initial research doc attached. We observed customer reports of spikes when naive retries are applied to streaming endpoints leading to duplicate tokens and cost spikes.

2026-03-03 - Diego Alvarez: PoC implemented three named profiles in TS SDK (latency-first, balanced, cost-first). Latency-first uses fast initial attempt with small jittered exponential, cost-first delays more aggressively and caps retries. Need to align exact constants across lang runtimes.

2026-03-05 - Samir Patel (Platform): Suggest adding an explicit header for idempotency scope: 'X-Redwood-Idemp-Scope' with allowed values 'request', 'session', 'stream-segment' to let routing layer determine safe dedupe windows. Also suggested 'resume-token' as first-class header for streaming resumes.

2026-03-07 - Design review (Lena Ortiz): UX note - examples should show both automatic id key generation helper and explicit developer-managed keys. Add migration callout for teams currently using message-level dedupe in app code.

2026-03-09 - Diego Alvarez: Decision log - defaults: latency-first (default for chat/interactive endpoints), balanced (default for official high-throughput text-generation), cost-first (default for embeddings/batch). Parameters (draft): latency-first = initial_delay 100ms, base_backoff 200ms, max_backoff 2s, max_retries 3; balanced = initial 200ms, base 400ms, max 5s, max_retries 4; cost-first = initial 500ms, base 1s, max 10s, max_retries 2. Values subject to fine-tuning after integration tests.

2026-03-10 - QA (Ivy Nguyen): Integration tests to cover: server 503 transient spikes, connection resets mid-stream, duplicate token suppression when idemp key reused within dedupe window. Need test harness that can simulate partial writes and resume tokens.

2026-03-11 - Diego Alvarez: Streaming semantics: For single-shot streams (e.g., short live audio->text), SDK will send 'X-Redwood-Idemp-Key' scoped to request unless user provides session key. For long-lived client sessions (conversation), SDK exposes session helpers that attach a persistent session id and 'stream-segment' when resuming. We will include a 'resume_token' in server responses; SDK will persist it and use it to distinguish true retries vs resumed segments.

2026-03-12 - Maya Chen: API ergonomics: Python helper will be idempotency_context(session_id=None, ttl_seconds=300) returning context manager that auto-generates per-request keys with optional prefix. TS/Go will include similar helpers with deterministic UUIDv5-based generation from session+sequence for deterministic replays.

2026-03-13 - Security (Arun Venkataraman): Review note - idempotency keys must not leak PII. Ensure generate helpers do not include raw user identifiers unless explicitly opted-in by developer. Recommend default to cryptographically-random keys and document trade-offs.

2026-03-14 - Diego Alvarez: Open tasks: finalize constants after running service-level chaos tests, add opt-in telemetry to capture retry profile used per-request (opt-out by default), write migration doc for customers using custom retry wrappers. Preparing PR for TS and Python with feature flags behind "stable-retries".
